title: Beatnik: A Novel Global Communication Mini-Application
problem: Existing benchmarks and mini-applications rarely exercise the complex communication patterns found in production HPC codes, making it difficult to evaluate communication system performance on modern platforms.
motivation: Understanding and optimizing communication patterns is critical for improving performance on modern GPU-accelerated HPC systems.
method: Beatnik creates a simplified model that simulates 3D Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities—a type of fluid flow mixing pattern—using the Z-Model mathematical formulation developed by Pandya and Shkoller. It runs within the Cabana framework, which allows the same code to run efficiently across different hardware types. The application provides four benchmark configurations to evaluate how well HPC communication systems (the networks and memory that move data between processors) perform under weak and strong scaling tests—where weak scaling adds more hardware while keeping the problem size per processor constant, and strong scaling adds more hardware to solve a fixed problem faster—on GPU-accelerated systems.
key_novelty: A mini-application that reproduces data-movement patterns from production HPC codes to expose communication bottlenecks—places where slow data transfer between processors limits overall performance—in modern accelerator-based systems.
contributions: Open-source Beatnik mini-application that exercises realistic communication patterns found in production codes
Four benchmark setups for comprehensive evaluation of HPC communication system performance
Demonstration of scalability on GPU systems up to 1024 GPUs with weak and strong scaling
Identification of communication challenges in modern systems and solver libraries
limitations: Specific limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: HPC communication mini-application for accelerator systems
